sources.title: Tosio Kato, Perturbation Theory for Linear Operators, 2nd ed.
sources.locator: Chapter II §1.3 “Perturbation of the resolvent,” §1.4 “Perturbation of the eigenprojections,” and §1.6 examples; printed pp. 66–69 and 71–72. Complete 643-page PDF was retrieved; the cited sections and adjacent proofs were inspected.
sources.support: Kato supplies the resolvent perturbation and isolated-cluster projector framework. Batch 97 derives its exact finite Hermitian gap radius, Frobenius derivative bound, residual Lipschitz constant, and discontinuity witness locally; no abstract Riesz projection theorem is imported.

contents.name: Chapter II §1.3, perturbation identity and local Neumann expansion for the resolvent
contents.support: The local proof writes and verifies the inverse identity for zI−H and derives the quadratic remainder and derivative integral with an explicit g-dependent bound.

contents.name: Chapter II §1.4, contour representation and perturbation of an isolated eigenprojection
contents.support: This is the source treatment closest to the total occupied block projector; the local proof independently diagonalizes the Hermitian matrix and evaluates the scalar contour integrals, retaining repeated eigenvalues within each block.

contents.name: Chapter II §1.6, examples of eigenprojection singularity at exceptional points
contents.support: The source records loss of regularity at spectral collisions; the local 2×2 path gives a direct two-sided limit calculation at a zero occupied gap.

full_text_read.method: Complete PDF previously downloaded to /tmp/pcscf-kato.pdf and extracted to /tmp/pcscf-kato.txt; inspected the complete relevant printed sections and proofs.
full_text_read.scope: Chapter II §§1.3–1.4 and §1.6, including the resolvent Neumann identity, contour formula for a total projection, and singular-projector examples.

retrieval_history.initial_attempt: The full PDF URL returned the complete Kato monograph; the full body was retained locally for inspection.
retrieval_history.recovery: No failed retrieval remained for this source.

sources.title: Benjamin Texier, “Basic matrix perturbation theory,” L’Enseignement Mathématique 64 (2018), 249–263.
sources.locator: §1 Proposition 1.1 and §2 Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 2.2, printed pp. 249–254 (15-page publisher PDF).
sources.support: This full-text expository note states continuity of finite-dimensional spectrum and the contour formula for total eigenprojectors. The local items specialize to Hermitian occupied clusters and prove all constants and derivative estimates themselves.

contents.name: §1 Proposition 1.1, continuity of eigenvalues as a multiset under continuous matrix perturbations
contents.reason: The batch uses the stronger Hermitian operator-norm Weyl estimate from batch 92 to obtain explicit gap radii; it does not import the general multiset-continuity statement.

contents.name: §2 Proposition 2.1, Cauchy formula for a total eigenprojector
contents.support: The source formula motivates the contour representation; the local proof derives it entrywise from the Hermitian spectral theorem and scalar Cauchy formulas, then differentiates the integral with an explicit remainder.

contents.name: §2 Corollary 2.2, regularity of an isolated eigenprojector
contents.support: The local theorem proves real Frechet C1 regularity and the concrete 16R/g² Frobenius derivative bound rather than importing the qualitative regularity claim.

contents.name: §§3–4, directional eigenvalue derivatives and Puiseux expansions at coalescence
contents.reason: The assigned pair makes no differentiability claim for individual eigenvalue branches and only treats a separated Hermitian block projector.

full_text_read.method: Opened the publisher-hosted full PDF at its direct PDF endpoint and inspected the complete relevant portions of §§1–2, including the full proof of Proposition 2.1.
full_text_read.scope: Complete relevant arguments for Proposition 1.1, Proposition 2.1, and Corollary 2.2; later eigenvalue-branch sections were not used.

retrieval_history.initial_attempt: Publisher direct PDF endpoint opened successfully as a 15-page PDF with full text.

sources.title: Eric Cancès and Claude Le Bris, “On the convergence of SCF algorithms for the Hartree–Fock equations,” M2AN 34 (2000), 749–774.
sources.locator: §2.2, printed pp. 756–763: Roothaan and level-shifting definitions, Theorem 7, and Example 9; §4, Theorem 11 on large level shifts. Complete 27-page PDF.
sources.support: This source distinguishes a strict spectral gap/well-posedness condition from convergence, exhibits oscillatory SCF behavior, and studies a different global level-shift algorithm. The local finite examples and block-ordering equivalence are independently proved.

contents.name: §2.2, Roothaan occupied-orbital update and strict HOMO–LUMO gap for unique aufbau selection
contents.support: The local response-map definition makes the same strict rth gap the exact domain condition, fixes ascending eigenvalue order, and proves uniqueness separately.

contents.name: Theorem 7 and its two-state oscillation alternative under uniform well-posedness
contents.support: The source establishes that SCF may oscillate even with well-posed orbital updates; the assigned finite 2×2 example has its own explicit matrix-by-matrix two-cycle proof and does not instantiate Theorem 7.

contents.name: Example 9, a Hartree–Fock Roothaan oscillation witness
contents.support: This is a literature comparison for the no-convergence warning; the local counterexample uses a separate finite-basis linear interaction and checks its gaps and updates exactly.

contents.name: §2.2 and §4, level-shifting algorithm and Theorem 11 on convergence for sufficiently large shifts
contents.reason: The assigned result is only the finite-dimensional algebraic equivalence for one fixed projector under commutation and strict shifted block ordering; the source theorem concerns a different iterative Hartree–Fock algorithm.

contents.name: §2.2, note that DIIS convergence was not established in this treatment
contents.reason: The local page gives no unconditional DIIS convergence theorem and instead proves its own residual safeguard; the historical literature-status observation is not used as a logical premise.

full_text_read.method: Complete Numdam PDF downloaded to /tmp/pcscf-cances-lebris-2000.pdf and extracted to /tmp/pcscf-cances-lebris-2000.txt; inspected all of §2.2 and Theorem 11 with its proof.
full_text_read.scope: §2.2 including Theorem 7, Example 9, and level-shift definitions; §4 Theorem 11 and proof.

sources.title: Eric Cancès, Gaspard Kemlin, and Antoine Levitt, “Convergence analysis of direct minimization and self-consistent iterations,” ESAIM: M2AN 54 (2020).
sources.locator: §2.1 on the projector manifold, §3.2 especially Theorem 3.4, and §4.4 with Appendix Lemma 4.1 on the convex hull of fixed-trace projectors; complete 41-page arXiv PDF.
sources.support: The source treats rank-N projector matrices and gives a model-specific convex-hull density set; Theorem 3.4 gives a local damped-SCF result with energy-Hessian and retraction assumptions. Batch 97 proves the complex projector/density facts locally and does not import the source’s specialized convergence conclusion.

contents.name: §2.1, fixed-trace Hermitian projector manifold M_N and projector convention
contents.support: The paper uses real symmetric projectors and notes the complex extension; the local lemma proves the Hermitian complex case directly from the spectral theorem.

contents.name: §4.4 and Appendix Lemma 4.1, convex hull CH(M_N) described by 0≤P≤I and fixed trace
contents.support: The source gives the density-matrix convex-hull convention in its finite-difference model; the local definition sets the same abstract Hermitian domain, and local items prove nonemptiness, closure, convexity, completeness, and projector inclusion.

contents.name: §4.4 and Appendix Lemma 4.1, compactness and convexity of the model-specific relaxed density set
contents.support: The paper establishes compactness and convexity for its finite-dimensional model. The local lemma supplies a direct sequence proof for arbitrary finite Hermitian dimension and Frobenius metric.

contents.name: §3.2, Theorem 3.4: local linear convergence of damped SCF with energy Hessian and retraction hypotheses
contents.reason: The theorem assumes a nondegenerate local minimizer, projected Hessian, retraction, positive gap, and sufficiently small damping; batch 97 instead proves contraction from an explicit induced derivative bound.

contents.name: §4.4, convex-hull density matrices include nonprojector interior mixtures
contents.support: The source identifies the fixed-trace positive-contraction hull; the local example computes I/2 directly from two orthogonal rank-one projectors and verifies it is admissible but not idempotent.

full_text_read.method: Complete PDF downloaded to /tmp/pcscf-cances-levitt.pdf and extracted to /tmp/pcscf-cances-levitt.txt; inspected all of §3.2 and the complete proof of Theorem 3.4.
full_text_read.scope: §2.1 projector-matrix conventions, complete §3.2 including Theorem 3.4 proof, and complete §4.4 plus the Appendix proof of Lemma 4.1 for the convex-hull density set.

retrieval_history.initial_attempt: The arXiv direct /pdf/ URL returned the complete PDF.

sources.title: Thorsten Rohwedder, An analysis for some methods and algorithms of quantum chemistry, doctoral thesis, TU Berlin.
sources.locator: Chapter 4 §4.1 “Notations and basic facts about DIIS,” printed pp. 95–97; §4.4 “Convergence analysis for DIIS,” beginning printed p. 110. Complete thesis PDF.
sources.support: The thesis supplies a full DIIS formulation and constrained residual least-squares objective. The local batch proves compact existence and unique minimum-norm selection for a finite coefficient cap, then gives explicit singular-solver and gap fallbacks; the thesis convergence theorem is not imported.

contents.name: §4.1, finite-history DIIS update and affine residual-minimization constraint
contents.support: The local algorithm adopts finite memory and affine residual minimization, and explicitly adds a coefficient 1-norm cap, singular/uncertified fallback, and projector-gap check.

contents.name: §4.1, Lagrange-multiplier bordered system for the coefficient minimization
contents.support: The finite example writes the bordered Gram matrix explicitly and shows duplicate rows; all singularity and fallback claims are verified by direct calculation.

contents.name: §4.4, Theorems 4.10 and 4.12: nonlinear DIIS convergence under Jacobian/preconditioner and linear-independence assumptions
contents.reason: Those local convergence hypotheses are not assumed by batch 97; the certified algorithm proves a separate fixed-point residual error inheritance theorem and makes no unconditional bare-DIIS claim.

full_text_read.method: Official TU Berlin full thesis downloaded to /tmp/pcscf-rohwedder-thesis.pdf and extracted to /tmp/pcscf-rohwedder-thesis.txt; inspected all of Chapter 4 §§4.1 and 4.4, including the relevant theorem assumptions.
full_text_read.scope: §4.1 DIIS definition and coefficient solve; §4.4 local convergence results and their complete assumptions.

sources.title: Homer F. Walker and Peng Ni, “Anderson Acceleration for Fixed-Point Iterations,” SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis 49 (2011), 1715–1735.
sources.locator: §1 for the fixed-point acceleration formulation; §2.2 Theorem 2.2 for the linear, untruncated equivalence result. Complete 21-page author PDF.
sources.support: This independent numerical-analysis article motivates residual-minimizing acceleration but sharply limits its theorem to a linear untruncated setting with nonsingularity and nonstagnation assumptions. Batch 97 does not use it as a nonlinear DIIS convergence theorem.

contents.name: §1, Anderson acceleration residual minimization and finite-history update
contents.support: The local DIIS proposal has the same affine residual-minimization motif, while its projector mixture, l1 cap, and fallback branches are fully specified locally.

contents.name: §2.2, Theorem 2.2: equivalence with GMRES for an untruncated linear fixed-point map under nonsingularity and nonstagnation
contents.reason: The theorem is restricted to untruncated linear problems and stated Krylov nonstagnation hypotheses; batch 97 makes no general nonlinear convergence claim for DIIS.
